The test image shows a soybean field with irregular, scattered patches of yellowing/dying plants interspersed within healthy green canopy — a classic field-level symptom pattern. Key observations:
- Patchy distribution of chlorotic/browning plants
- Irregular patch shapes scattered across the field
- Otherwise healthy-looking green plants surrounding affected areas

This strongly suggests either Soybean Cyst Nematode (patches + stunting + chlorosis) or Sudden Death Syndrome. Let me check the SCN reference.

The reference SCN image (top-right panel) shows the exact same pattern as the test image: irregular, scattered patches of yellowing/chlorotic plants within an otherwise green soybean canopy. This field-level patchy distribution is the hallmark of SCN — "symptomatic plants usually occur in patches and show stunting, slow or no canopy closure, and chlorotic foliage."
